clue.text: Instrument physician used to probe Olivia's attendant

indicators.note: something used to probe goes inside what it examines, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Maria is Olivia's waiting-gentlewoman in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a physician's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor uses some musical instrument to examine a lady's maid.
explanation.walkthrough: Olivia and Maria are characters from Twelfth Night; the doctor's letters slip into the maid's name near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: The marimba is a percussion instrument of tuned wooden bars, a kind of xylophone.

clue.text: Principal river in Germany

definitions.meaning: chief or most important, as in the chief road
the ... flows through Frankfurt to join the Rhine

explanation.definitionFit: Main means chief or principal, and is also the name of a major German river.

clue.text: Pay further call on vicar, questioning identity?

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
asking 'is it?' questions who or what something is

explanation.surface: A clergyman doing his rounds again, unsure if he has the right house.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit is to go back to a person or place, calling on them once more.

clue.text: The value of some ritual

indicators.note: letters taken out of the following words, as part of them, signal a run lying inside

explanation.surface: A remark on the worth of a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence, the value something holds.

clue.text: Appropriate anger father displayed over drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, displayed over means the whole string is set out bottom to top, read in reverse

parts.note: fit means suitable or appropriate
ire is anger
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A father shows his anger, rightly, over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'displayed over' means the three joined synonyms are read upwards, so the whole string is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: A platform for the beak

definitions.meaning: a raised stand for a speaker or conductor
in zoology a ... is a bird's bill or similar snout

explanation.surface: A dais set up for the magistrate, 'beak' being slang for a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' suggests a magistrate in the dock scene, but here it is a bird's bill, the zoological sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostrum means both a speaker's raised stage and, in biology, a beak-like snout.

clue.text: Royal duke abandons plan to give up office

indicators.note: the duke abandoning the plan means his letter leaves that word

parts.note: a design is a plan

explanation.surface: A royal duke drops his scheme in order to quit his post.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a job or office voluntarily.

clue.text: South American sailor taken round by top celebrity

indicators.note: the American letters are taken round the next word, enclosing it

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US forces
per means by, as in per post
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman from South America is shown around by a famous star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one idea, but it splits into two pieces, and 'taken round' applies to the American part alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstar is an extremely famous performer, a celebrity of the highest rank.

clue.text: Made reparation for altering the grid

indicators.note: altering the grid changes the order of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone fixed a mistake by changing the crossword grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To have righted a wrong is to have put it right, making amends for it.

clue.text: Profitable undertaking for one producing bread?

definitions.meaning: a venture that earns a lot of cash
bread is slang for cash, so a producer of it is someone who generates income

explanation.definitionFit: A moneymaker is a lucrative venture, and literally someone who makes bread in the slang sense of cash.

clue.text: Trendy son carrying French novelist's overcoat

indicators.note: the first pieces carry the novelist's name inside them

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
Jules Verne, French author of Around the World in Eighty Days, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A fashionable young man wears a coat belonging to a French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on 'novelist's' supplies a letter, so the author's name keeps its S.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inverness is a sleeveless overcoat with a cape, named after the Scottish town.

clue.text: Pantheistic violinist missing in island

indicators.note: the violinist's name is missing the letters of the next words

parts.note: Niccolo Paganini was a virtuoso Italian violinist
taken as written
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A nature-worshipping fiddler has gone missing on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing IN and I from the end of PAGANINI leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagan beliefs worship many gods or nature itself, which is close to pantheism.

clue.text: Like a model well-placed financially?

definitions.meaning: an artist's model sits looking attractive for the painter
an idiom for being comfortably off or in an advantageous position

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being in a fortunate position, and literally describes a model posing attractively.

clue.text: Language used when Indian's hut collapses

indicators.note: a collapsing hut falls into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some Indian speech is heard when a shack falls down.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindustani is a language of northern India, the common base of Hindi and Urdu.

clue.text: Fearless, popular and cool in suppressing resistance

parts.note: in means popular, as in the in crowd

indicators.note: the cool word suppresses, holding down within it, the letter for resistance

parts.note: tepid means lukewarm, rather cool
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A brave, well-liked, calm figure puts down opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' suggests calm composure but here means lukewarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means bold and undaunted, without fear.

clue.text: Basic points connected with Latin translation

parts.note: E, S, S, E: compass points east, south, south, east

indicators.note: translation renders a word in new form, here rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: The fundamental points of a Latin translation exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' as four compass letters is a crossword habit; 'translation' rearranges the language name into NTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential means fundamental or basic, at the core of something.

clue.text: Way a supporter rejected sports arenas

parts.note: St, short for Street, is a way

indicators.note: a rejected item is sent back, so the supporter word is turned backwards

parts.note: an aid is a helper or support

explanation.surface: A fan is turned away from the stadiums.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is the Latin plural of stadium, a venue for sports events.

clue.text: Tribal head establishing preserve in African country

indicators.note: the preserve sits in the country's name

parts.note: Benin is a West African country
jam is a fruit preserve

explanation.surface: A chief sets up a nature reserve in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'establishing' is only a link here; 'Tribal head' looks like a chief but means a founder of one of Israel's tribes.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin, youngest son of Jacob, was founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

clue.text: Stop someone believing son has been arrested

indicators.note: the son is arrested, held inside the believer's word

parts.note: a deist believes in God from reason, without revealed religion

explanation.surface: A believer's son is taken into custody and told to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or stop doing something.

clue.text: Shades of the hard stuff?

definitions.meaning: ghosts or phantoms of the dead
strong alcohol such as whisky or gin

explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are ghosts, called shades in poetry, and also distilled liquor.

clue.text: Drink bishop imbibed at Paddington is just about OK

indicators.note: the drink with its bishop is placed at, beside, the bear

parts.note: Paddington is the famous bear of children's books

indicators.note: the drink has imbibed, taken in, the letter for bishop

parts.note: ale is a drink
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman drinking beer in a London station is passable.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is a London station, but here the children's-book bear. B goes into ALE to make ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearable means tolerable, just about acceptable.

clue.text: Youngster has bed, say, to send to Coventry

parts.note: a boy is a youngster

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken, the spelling chosen for its sound

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A lad has a bed, perhaps, in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them; COTT is pronounced like 'cot'.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott is to shun or refuse dealings with, as sending someone to Coventry does.

clue.text: One is often cast as a relay runner

definitions.meaning: a ship's weight, thrown overboard to hold it
the final runner in a relay team

explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is thrown from a ship to hold it, and the last leg of a relay is run by the anchor.

clue.text: Giddy girl's machine for making thread

parts.note: spinning means dizzy or giddy
Jenny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A dizzy young woman owns a device for producing yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning jenny was Hargreaves's multi-spindle machine for spinning thread.

clue.text: Prickly growth father found in middle of knoll

indicators.note: the father is found inside the letters taken from the knoll
the middle of a word is all of it without its first and last letters

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Dad stumbles on a thorny plant in the middle of a hillock.
explanation.definitionFit: The nopal is a prickly-pear cactus, a spiny plant of Mexico.

clue.text: In which things occur simultaneously and decline in sound?

indicators.note: in sound means as spoken, the word heard rather than read

parts.note: to sink is to decline or drop

explanation.surface: A question about events happening at once and fading in volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Sync, short for synchronisation, describes events occurring at the same time.

clue.text: Bail unexpectedly secured by one's defence

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are secured by, fastened next to, the numeral
unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Unexpected bail is obtained by someone's legal defence.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence that the accused was elsewhere when the crime happened.

clue.text: Many work hard on vessel without music

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the vessel encloses the rest

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel
M, Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
op, short for opus, is a work
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd toils on a boat with no music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: HOY surrounds MOPHON.
explanation.definitionFit: Homophony is music in which one melody is supported by chords moving with it.

clue.text: Blinkered? Man may be thus described

definitions.meaning: narrow-minded, seeing little of the world
the Isle of Man is an island, so the word for island-like applies

explanation.surface: Is a man blinkered, and might he be called so?
explanation.definitionFit: Insular means narrow in outlook, and literally of an island like the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Nothing to do with the ear or tongue of Africans

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero
otic is the medical adjective for relating to the ear

explanation.surface: Something unrelated to either hearing or African speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic names a group of languages spoken by peoples of the Nile valley in East Africa.
